q: What does the b at the end of Hmoob tell you?
o: Say a b sound at the end
why: The last letter is a tone letter: -b marks the high tone, and it is never said.

q: A syllable has no tone letter at all, like zoo (good). How is it said?
o: Flat, in your normal speaking voice
why: No tone letter means the mid tone: flat, your normal speaking voice.

q: dej means water. What does dev mean?
o: Dog: a different tone letter makes a different word
why: dej has the falling tone and dev the rising tone; they are two different words.

q: How is the x in xav (to think) said?
why: In RPA x is an English s sound; s is the sh-like sound.

q: What is the w in tw (tail)?
o: A consonant, as in English we
A vowel, like the i of roses with spread lips
why: w is always a vowel in Hmong, never a consonant.

q: What does the h in ph, th, kh and qh show?
o: Say ph as f and th as in think
A puff of air after the consonant
why: An h after a consonant makes it aspirated: a puff of air follows.

q: How does the np in npua (pig) start?
o: With a short hum through the nose, like mb
Like English n, then a separate p
why: np is pre-nasalised: a quick hum, then the p, like the mb of number.

q: What is the difference between nab and hnab?
o: None: two spellings of one word
hnab starts breathy and means bag; nab is snake
why: hn is a breathy n, and it makes a different word: hnab, bag.

q: In neeg (person), what does the double e show?
o: A g sound at the end
A nasal vowel, close to eng
why: A doubled vowel is nasal: ee is close to eng, with no g said.

q: It's 8 a.m. and you meet a neighbor. What do you say?
why: Nyob zoo works at any time of day; Hmong has no separate good morning.

q: Someone says Ua tsaug to you. What is a natural reply?
why: Tsis ua li cas, it's nothing, answers thanks.

q: What does os do at the end of Pw zoo os?
o: It makes the sentence a question
It is the word for night
It softens the sentence and sounds warm
why: os is a softening word at the end of a sentence.

q: You are talking about yourself and one friend. Which word means 'we'?
why: wb is exactly two people; peb is three or more.

q: What does nws mean?
why: nws covers he, she and it.

q: Which word means 'you' for three or more people?
why: koj is one person, neb two, nej three or more.

q: How do you say 'I'm happy'?
why: A describing word needs no yog: Kuv zoo siab.

q: Which word fills 'Kuv ___ hauv lub tsev' (I'm in the house)?
why: nyob is for where someone is.

q: What does Nov yog lub tsev mean?
why: Nov is this, yog says what it is, lub tsev is the house.

q: Where does puas go in a yes-or-no question?
why: puas sits right before the verb: Koj puas hais lus Askiv?

q: How do you ask 'Where do you want to go?'
why: The question word stays where the answer goes, after the verb mus.

q: What does los tsis yog add at the end of a sentence?
why: los tsis yog means or not? and turns a statement into a yes-or-no question.

q: Where does tsis go?
o: At the end of the sentence
At the very start, before the person
why: tsis comes right before the verb: Kuv tsis paub.

q: How do you say 'Don't go!'?
why: Don't is tsis txhob, before the verb.

q: Someone asks Koj puas paub? (Do you know?) and you don't. You say…
why: tsis before the verb paub: Kuv tsis paub.

q: What is missing in 'Kuv npe hu ua Paj'?
why: npe (name) needs its classifier: Kuv lub npe hu ua Paj.

q: How do you ask 'Where are you from?'
why: tuaj sits on both sides of the place word: Koj tuaj qhov twg tuaj?

q: In Kuv lub npe hu ua Paj, which words mean 'is called'?
why: hu ua means is called; lub npe is the name.

q: How do you say 20?
why: Twenty has its own word: nees nkaum. kaum ob is 12.

q: Which one is 60?
why: After six, seven, eight and nine the tens word is caum, with the creaky tone letter m.

q: What is kaum ob?
why: kaum (ten) comes first, then the extra: ten and two.

q: Where does the classifier go in 'two houses'?
o: After the noun: ob tsev lub
Before the number: lub ob tsev
Between the number and the noun: ob lub tsev
why: Number, then classifier, then noun: ob lub tsev.

q: Which classifier goes with kaus (umbrella)?
why: Umbrellas take lub, not tus: lub kaus.

q: What is the difference between daim ntawv and phau ntawv?
o: A sheet of paper and a book
why: daim counts flat things (a sheet of paper); phau counts books.

q: How do you say 'the red car'?
why: Classifier and noun first, then the describing word: lub tsheb liab.

q: Where does no (this) go?
o: At the very end of the noun phrase
Between the classifier and the noun
why: This and that come last: lub tsev no, lub tsev loj no.

q: In kuv lub tsheb, where does 'my' go?
o: Hmong has no word for my
why: The owner goes first: kuv lub tsheb.

q: A woman talks about her brother. Which word does she use?
why: A woman calls any brother nus; kwv and tij laug are said by a man.

q: A man talks about his sister. Which word does he use?
why: A man says muam; a woman says viv ncaus.

q: What is phauj?
why: phauj is your father's sister; dab laug is your mother's brother.

q: How does Hmong show that something happened yesterday?
o: With a time word such as nag hmo; the verb stays the same
The verb moves to the end
With a different tone on the verb
why: Hmong verbs never change; nag hmo (yesterday) tells you when.

q: What does tag kis mean?
why: tag kis is tomorrow; nag hmo is yesterday and hnub no is today.

q: What is kaum ob hlis ntuj?
why: Months are numbered: twelve + hlis ntuj is December.

q: Where does lawm go?
o: At the start of the sentence
After the verb and its object
Between the subject and the verb
why: lawm follows the verb and its object: Kuv noj mov lawm.

q: What does tab tom show?
o: The action is going on now
why: tab tom means 'in the middle of': Lawv tab tom haus dej.

q: In Kuv yuav yuav ib lub tsheb, what does the second yuav mean?
why: The first yuav is 'will', the second is the verb 'buy'.

q: Which word means 'up there' (higher than you)?
why: pem is up there; nram is down there.

q: How do you say 'The book is on the table'?
why: Location takes nyob, then saum and the place.

q: What is tod?
o: The form of tom at the end of a phrase
why: At the end of a phrase tom becomes tod.

q: Which verb goes with dej (water)?
why: Drinks take haus: Kuv haus dej.

q: What does noj mov mean?
why: noj mov, literally 'eat rice', is to eat a meal.

q: How do you say 'chicken' (the meat)?
why: nqaij (meat) + qaib (chicken): nqaij qaib.

q: How do you say 'I'm going out to buy vegetables'?
why: The verbs sit side by side, with no thiab: mus yuav.

q: In Kuv muab phau ntawv rau koj, who gets the book?
why: The person after rau gets the thing.

q: Where does yuav (will) go in a row of verbs?
o: At the end of the sentence
why: yuav goes before the first verb: Kuv yuav mus yuav nqaij npua.

q: Where does thov (please) go?
o: At the very end of the sentence
why: thov goes right before the action: Thov zaum, Thov pab kuv.

q: You want to tell a child "Don't eat." Which word goes before noj?
why: tsis txhob before the verb means don't: Tsis txhob noj.

q: What does puas tau? do at the end of a sentence?
o: It turns it into a polite "may I / could you?"
why: Pab kuv puas tau? = Could you help me? Kuv nug puas tau? = May I ask?

q: How do you say "I'm happy"?
why: No yog before a feeling: the feeling word is the verb.

q: What does Hnub no los nag mean?
why: hnub no = today, los nag = to rain.

q: Which word means "warm"?
why: sov is warm; no is cold, cua is wind and nag is rain.

q: How do you ask "How much is this?"
why: pes tsawg stays at the end, where the answer goes.

q: Which means "two pairs of shoes"?
why: Shoes are counted in pairs with nkawm, between the number and the noun.

q: What does pheej yig mean?
why: pheej yig is cheap; kim is expensive.

q: How do you say "I have a headache"?
why: mob works as the verb, and the body part comes right after it.

q: What does noj tshuaj mean?
why: Hmong eats medicine: noj tshuaj.

q: Which counting word goes with kws kho mob (doctor)?
why: People take tus: tus kws kho mob.

q: Where does tshaj go?
why: Describing word first, then tshaj: loj tshaj.

q: What does Kuv laus tshaj koj mean?
why: The first thing (kuv) is the one that is more: older than you.

q: "very big" is…
why: heev goes after the describing word.

q: Your grandmother has just arrived. What do you say?
why: Koj tuaj los? greets someone who has just come.

q: Grandpa asks if you have eaten. You haven't yet. You say…
why: tsis tau goes before the verb: not yet.

q: When do you say Mus ho tuaj?
why: Mus ho tuaj, come again, is said to a departing guest.

q: What is noj peb caug?
why: noj peb caug is the New Year celebration.

q: Which word means "throw"?
why: pov has the rising tone (-v): throw. pob is a ball.

q: "new clothes" is…
why: The describing word comes after the noun.

q: What is a xeem?
o: a clan, which is also the surname
why: xeem is clan; xeev, with a different tone letter, is a state.

q: "I have two children" is…
why: People take tus, written tug after ob.

q: What is khi tes?
o: a blessing with strings on the wrist
why: Elders tie strings around the wrist and wish the person health.
